newsitem.title: JAPAN: BT to boost Japan business, eyes ties with NTT.
newsitem.headline: BT to boost Japan business, eyes ties with NTT.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc made clear on Thursday it would boost its Japanese business, adding that Japanese telecom giant NTT Corp is a viable partner for its global strategy.
"One of BT's highest company-wide priorities is success in the Japanese market," John Jarvis, the chief of BT's Japanese unit, told a news conference.
Jarvis said that BT's relationship with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp is "very positive", citing a joint bid for a second national telecom licence in Singapore.
This view was echoed by Alfred Mockett, managing director of another BT unit, BT Global Communications, who also attended Thursday's news conference.
"As a market in the early stages of liberalisation, it's important for us to consider all business opportunities in Japan...not the least of which is our relationship with NTT," he said.
BT, with its U.S. partner MCI Communications Corp, has been trying to gain a foothold in the lucrative Asian market for years and has been openly courting NTT.
Asia remains the last gap in BT's and MCI's global jigsaw of deals.
NTT, however, has pursued a go-it-alone stance, stating that collaboration with BT in Singapore should not be taken as a sign of a wider relationship.

Asked if there is a discrepancy in views between NTT and BT, Mockett said: "We don't see this as a sign of discrepancy... I wouldn't discount a possibility of (BT and NTT) seizing other similar future opportunities."
A source close to one of BT's French partners, a unit of Cie Generale des Eau, told Reuters in London recently that NTT was considering a 9.9 percent stake in another CGE unit, Telecom Developpement.
But an NTT official, who asked not to be identified, said NTT so far had no plans to acquire telecom facilities in Europe.
"It's risky to have our own facilities in Europe from the beginning. We plan to lease them to start with," he said.

BT's planned merger with MCI, the second-biggest U.S. telephone company, will create a global giant with combined annual revenues of $42 billion, but this accounts for only six percent of the global market, Mockett said.
"A big piece of opportunities comes from Japan," he said adding that BT considers NTT a viable partner.
Mockett said BT aims to nearly double revenues at its Japanese unit to $176 million over the next two years.
The Japanese unit, BT Network Information Service (BT NIS), was established on April 1 jointly with Japan's Marubeni Corp and aims to achieve $97 million in revenues in the year that started April 1.
BT in March streamlined its Japanese operations, combining its existing joint venture, NIS, and the BT group's Japanese unit, BT Japan, to provide domestic and global communications services.
